partners.mechanism_chain: BEST1 (HGNC:1060) —DISRUPTS→ Retinal dysfunction (HP:0007770); Retinal dysfunction (HP:0007770) —LEADS_TO→ Vitreoretinal degeneration (HP:0000557); SCNN1A (HGNC:10671) —DISRUPTS→ Epithelial sodium channel activity (GO:0005251); Epithelial sodium channel activity (GO:0005251) —LEADS_TO→ Electrolyte imbalance (HP:0003103); Epithelial sodium channel activity (GO:0005251) —LEADS_TO→ Hypertension (HP:0000822). Mutations in BEST1 lead to haploinsufficiency, disrupting retinal function and causing vitreoretinal degeneration. Mutations in SCNN1A cause loss-of-function, impairing epithelial sodium channel activity, leading to electrolyte imbalances and hypertension, which are hallmarks of pseudohypoaldosteronism type IB1. While BEST1 is primarily involved in retinal pigment epithelium function and ion transport, and SCNN1A in the epithelial sodium channel, both genes' dysregulation impact cellular ion homeostasis and ultimately manifest as distinct but mechanistically related disease phenotypes.

#### 1. malignant hyperthermia, susceptibility to, 1  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.400)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2672351)

**Proposed mechanism:** RYR1 variant (rs1800348) —DISRUPTS→ RYR1 (HGNC:10194); RYR1 (HGNC:10194) —INCREASES→ Sarcoplasmic Reticulum Calcium Release (GO:0030049); Sarcoplasmic Reticulum Calcium Release (GO:0030049) —LEADS_TO→ Malignant Hyperthermia Susceptibility (HP:0003327); Sarcoplasmic Reticulum Calcium Release (GO:0030049) —LEADS_TO→ Altered Cellular Calcium Levels (HP:0003327); BEST1 variant (rs121918346) —DISRUPTS→ BEST1 (HGNC:1199); BEST1 (HGNC:1199) —DISRUPTS→ Epithelial Calcium Homeostasis (GO:0007205); Epithelial Calcium Homeostasis (GO:0007205) —LEADS_TO→ Vitreoretinochoroidopathy (HP:0011260); Epithelial Calcium Homeostasis (GO:0007205) —LEADS_TO→ Altered Cellular Calcium Levels (HP:0003327). Gain-of-function mutations in RYR1 lead to aberrant calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum, manifesting as malignant hyperthermia susceptibility. Similarly, gain-of-function mutations in BEST1 disrupt epithelial calcium homeostasis, leading to vitreoretinochoroidopathy. Both pathways converge on the disruption of normal cellular calcium levels, impacting distinct but related cellular processes.

**How to falsify it:** The absence of gain-of-function mutations in both RYR1 and BEST1 in patients with the respective phenotypes, or the identification of distinct, non-overlapping molecular pathways that do not involve calcium dysregulation for each disease. _(variant: rs1800348, rs121918346)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of calcium homeostasis dysregulation in these two distinct diseases could potentially lead to therapeutic strategies targeting calcium channel modulation or buffering, applicable to both conditions.

Pathogenic variants in BEST1 (associated with vitreoretinochoroidopathy) and SCNN1A (associated with Liddle syndrome 3) both disrupt the regulation of epithelial sodium channels, leading to distinct downstream cellular dysfunctions and phenotypes.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a pathogenic variant in SCNN1A in patients diagnosed with autosomal dominant vitreoretinochoroidopathy, or conversely, a pathogenic variant in BEST1 in patients diagnosed with Liddle syndrome 3, would falsify the proposed distinct genetic origins converging on epithelial sodium channel regulation. _(variant: gnomad v2.1.1 shows SCNN1A variants with allele frequencies > 0.01% in European populations.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanistic principle of disrupted epithelial sodium channel regulation, despite different causal genes, could reveal novel therapeutic targets for both retinal degenerations and salt-sensitive hypertension.
